rule_statement: Level 4 = Tertiary Prevention / Survivor. It reflects a prior major cardiovascular or cerebrovascular event and is not an emergency category.
approved_statement: Validated: Level 4 is an immutable baseline prevention category for survivors of major cardiovascular/cerebrovascular events. Acute or unstable symptoms are handled separately through the Red Flag pathway.
notes: Do not use Level 4 to represent current acute instability.
source_automation_status: Safe as fixed logic once qualifying events are validated; live acute symptoms use separate Red Flag routing

rule_statement: S = Special coaching modifier. It is a dynamic flag, separate from Prevention Level 1–4 and separate from the Red Flag pathway. It applies when a significant medical, psychosocial, family, financial, occupational, caregiving or other life circumstance creates sustained stress, reduces self-efficacy, or materially affects the feasibility of standard coaching or pledges.
approved_statement: Validated for MVP: S is recorded as Active/Inactive; it does not alter the underlying Prevention Level. Its purpose is to trigger adapted coaching, pledge selection/intensity, empathic support and follow-up. Acute safety concerns belong to the separate Red Flag pathway. Remote/minor surgery does not automatically qualify. Ambiguous triggers remain human-reviewed initially.
notes: Preserve longitudinal episode history. Retire earlier assumptions that S means Structural/Safety/Surgical, that every surgery qualifies, that S is permanent once set, or that acute symptoms are S by default.
source_automation_status: Rule-assisted for clear predefined contexts; ambiguous activation/deactivation requires human review initially

rule_statement: Red Flag is a separate acute safety/escalation pathway, independent of Prevention Level and S. Explicit validated symptoms/thresholds stop routine coaching and trigger urgent/emergency review.
approved_statement: Validated conceptually: Red Flag is separate from Level 1–4 and S. Use approved urgency categories; live cases route to a person/clinical service.
notes: Red Flag must not be encoded as Level 4 or as S.
source_automation_status: Deterministic flagging allowed after validation; live clinical response requires human/clinical routing

rule_statement: Stop routine coaching at confirmed BP ≥180 systolic and/or ≥120 diastolic. Repeat after at least 1 minute; without acute symptoms arrange same-day clinical contact; with concerning acute symptoms use emergency pathway.
approved_statement: Validated for MVP training. Live cases may be flagged automatically but clinical action routes to a person/service.
notes: Keep BP measurement technique distinct from escalation logic.
source_automation_status: Automatic recognition/scoring in training; live cases human/clinical routing

rule_statement: Volunteer may assist with basic first-response for mild suspected/confirmed hypoglycaemia only when caregiver is conscious, cooperative and can swallow safely; severe/unsafe cases require emergency help.
approved_statement: Validated for MVP training; severe or ambiguous live cases must route to a person/emergency pathway.
notes: Any oral treatment or glucagon rules must remain within approved volunteer scope.
source_automation_status: Automatic scoring of clear training scenarios; live severe/ambiguous cases human/emergency routing
